title.zh: 卷一百八十二 列傳第六十九: 張起巖 歐陽玄 許有壬 宋本 謝端
title.en: Volume 182 Biographies 69: Zhang Qiyan, ŌUyang Xuan, Xu Youren, Song Ben, Xie Duan
title.raw: 卷一百八十二 列傳第六十九: 張起巖 歐陽玄 許有壬 宋本 謝端 Volume 182 Biographies 69: Zhang Qiyan, ŌUyang Xuan, Xu Youren, Song Ben, Xie Duan

sentences.zh: 張起岩

translations.literal: Zhang Qiyan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiyan

sentences.zh: 張起岩，字夢臣。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiyan, styled Mengchen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiyan, whose style was Mengchen.

sentences.zh: 其先章丘人，五季避地禹城。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Zhangqiu; in the Five Dynasties they moved to Yucheng to escape turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: His family came from Zhangqiu; during the Five Dynasties they fled the turmoil and settled in Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖迪，以元帥右監軍權濟南府事，徙家濟南。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Di, as Deputy Military Superintendent on the right wing of the commandery army, held temporary charge of Jinan prefectural affairs and moved the household to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Di served as deputy military superintendent on the commandery army's right wing, acted as temporary administrator of Jinan prefecture, and moved the family there.

sentences.zh: 當金之季，張榮據有章丘、鄒平、濟陽、長山、辛市、蒲台、新城、淄州之地，歲丙戌，歸於太祖，始終能效忠節，迪與其子福，實先後羽翼之。

translations.literal: In the late Jin, Zhang Rong held Zhangqiu, Zouping, Jiyang, Changshan, Xinshi, Putai, Xincheng, and Zizhou. In the year bingxu he submitted to Taizu and to the end was able to show loyal constancy; Di and his son Fu were in fact those who supported him first and last.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin dynasty Zhang Rong controlled Zhangqiu, Zouping, Jiyang, Changshan, Xinshi, Putai, Xincheng, and Zizhou. In the bingxu year he submitted to Taizu and remained loyal to the end; Di and his son Fu were among those who had supported him from the beginning.

sentences.zh: 福仕為濟南路軍民鎮撫兵鈐轄，權府事，生東昌錄事判官鐸，鐸生四川行省儒學副提舉範，範生起岩。

translations.literal: Fu served as Military and Civil Pacification Commissioner of Jinan Circuit and as Controller of Troops, acting in prefectural affairs; he begot Duo, Recorder and Administrator of Dongchang; Duo begot Fan, Associate Director of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat Confucian School; Fan begot Qiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu held the posts of Jinan circuit military and civil pacification commissioner and troop controller, with acting charge of prefectural affairs. His son Duo became recorder-administrator of Dongchang; Duo's son Fan became associate director of the Sichuan branch secretariat Confucian school; Fan was Qiyan's father.

sentences.zh: 初，其母丘氏有娠，見長蛇數丈入榻下，已忽不見，乃驚而誕起岩。

translations.literal: At first, when his mother the Lady Qiu was pregnant, she saw a serpent many zhang long enter beneath the couch, then suddenly it was gone; startled, she gave birth to Qiyan.
translations.idiomatic: While his mother Lady Qiu was pregnant, she saw a serpent many zhang long slip under the couch and then vanish. Startled by the omen, she gave birth to Qiyan.

sentences.zh: 幼從其父學，年弱冠，以察舉為福山縣學教諭，值縣官捕蝗，移攝縣事。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under his father; at the weak-crown year he was nominated by investigation and appointed instructor at the Fushan county school. When the county magistrate went to catch locusts, he was transferred to act as county administrator.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied with his father. In his early twenties he was nominated and appointed instructor at the Fushan county school. When the magistrate left to conduct locust control, Qiyan was left to act as county administrator.

sentences.zh: 久之，聽斷明允，其民相率曰：「若得張教諭為真縣尹，吾屬何患焉。」

translations.literal: After a long while his judgments were clear and fair; the people together said: "If we could have Instructor Zhang as the true county magistrate, what would we have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long his decisions proved clear and fair, and the people said as one: "If Instructor Zhang were our real magistrate, what would we have to fear?"

sentences.zh: 政成，遷安丘。

translations.literal: When his administration was accomplished, he was transferred to Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When his term succeeded, he was transferred to Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 中延祐乙卯進士，首選，除同知登州事，特旨改集賢修撰，轉國子博士，升國子監丞，進翰林待制，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the yimao year of the Yanyou reign he passed the jinshi examination as top choice; he was appointed Associate Administrator of Dengzhou, then by special edict made Compiler in the Hall of Gathered Talents, transferred to Erudite of the National University, promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, advanced to Hanlin Attendant-Drafter, and concurrently made Compiler of the National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year of Yanyou he took the jinshi degree as first in his class. He was appointed associate administrator of Dengzhou, then by special edict made a compiler in the Hall of Gathered Talents, became an erudite of the National University, rose to vice director of the directorate of education, and was promoted to Hanlin attendant-drafter with a concurrent post as national history compiler.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，選為監察御史。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was selected as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he observed mourning, and when the mourning ended he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 中書參政楊廷玉以墨敗，台臣奉旨就廟堂逮之下吏。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Associate Administrator Yang Tingyu was ruined by corruption; the censors, by imperial order, arrested him in the hall of government and handed him to the judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: Associate administrator of the central secretariat Yang Tingyu fell to a corruption case. By imperial order the censors arrested him in the council hall and turned him over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 丞相倒剌沙疾其摧辱同列，悉誣台臣罔上，欲置之重辟。

translations.literal: Chancellor Daula Shah resented their humiliation of his colleagues, wholly slandered the censors for deceiving the throne, and wished to impose severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Daula Shah resented the humiliation of his colleagues and accused the entire censorate of deceiving the throne, seeking to have them punished with the heaviest penalties.

sentences.zh: 起岩以新除留台，抗章論曰：「台臣按劾百官，論列朝政，職使然也。

translations.literal: Qiyan, having been newly appointed and remaining at the censorate, submitted a memorial in protest saying: 'Censors investigate and impeach the hundred officials and discuss court policy—that is what their office requires.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan had just been appointed and was still at the censorate. He submitted a forceful memorial arguing: "Censors investigate officials and debate court policy because that is their duty.

sentences.zh: 今以奉職獲戾，風紀解體，正直結舌，忠良寒心，殊非盛世事。

translations.literal: Now to be punished for performing one's duty—discipline collapses, the upright are silenced, the loyal and good are chilled at heart; this is far from what a flourishing age should see.
translations.idiomatic: To punish them for doing their jobs will break down discipline, silence the upright, and chill the hearts of the loyal. That is no way to run a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 且世皇建臺閣，廣言路，維持治體，陛下即位詔旨，動法祖宗。

translations.literal: Moreover Shizu established the censorate and broadened the avenue of speech to sustain the governing order; Your Majesty's accession edicts constantly follow the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Emperor Shizu established the censorate and opened the channels of remonstrance to sustain good government, and Your Majesty's accession edicts repeatedly invoke the example of the founding ancestors.

sentences.zh: 今台臣坐譴，公論杜塞，何謂法祖宗耶！」

translations.literal: Now the censors sit under reprimand and public opinion is blocked—what is this called, following the ancestors?'
translations.idiomatic: Now the censors are being punished and public opinion is shut out—how is that following the ancestors!"

sentences.zh: 章三上，不報。

translations.literal: He submitted the memorial three times without response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the memorial three times and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 起岩廷爭愈急，帝感悟，事乃得釋，猶皆坐罷免還鄉里。

translations.literal: Qiyan argued in court with growing urgency; the emperor was moved to understanding, and the affair was released, yet all still sat under dismissal and returned to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan pressed his case in court with growing urgency until the emperor was moved. The crisis was averted, but the censors were still dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 遷中書右司員外郎，進左司郎中，兼經筵官，拜太子右贊善。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat, advanced to Director of the Left Department, concurrently made Lecturer at the Classics Mat, and appointed Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made outer gentleman of the central secretariat's right department, then director of the left department, with a concurrent post as classics mat lecturer, and was appointed right assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服除，改燕王府司馬，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father; when the mourning ended he was changed to Chief Commandant of the Prince of Yan's establishment and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, and when it ended he became chief commandant of the Prince of Yan's household and was appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 文宗親郊，起岩充大禮使，導帝陟降，步武有節，衣前後襜如，陪位百官，望之如古圖畫中所睹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong personally performed the suburban sacrifice, Qiyan served as Grand Master of Rites, guiding the emperor in ascent and descent; his steps had measure, his robes before and behind hung even, and the officials in attendance, looking at him, seemed to see what is shown in ancient paintings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong performed the suburban sacrifice in person, Qiyan served as grand master of rites and guided the emperor's ascent and descent. His pace was measured, his robes hung evenly fore and aft, and the officials in attendance thought they were looking at a figure from an ancient painting.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之，賜賚優渥。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised him and bestowed rewards in generous measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 轉參議中書省事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Councilor of Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to councilor of central secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 寧宗崩，燕南俄起大獄，有妄男子上變，言部使者謀不軌，按問皆虛，法司謂：「《唐律》，告叛者不反坐。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong died, Yan South soon saw a great case arise: a reckless man submitted an accusation saying a circuit envoy plotted sedition; investigation showed it all false. The judicial office said: "In the 《Tang Code》, one who reports rebellion is not punished in turn."
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ningzong died, a major case soon erupted in the Yan region. A reckless man filed a report accusing a circuit envoy of sedition, but investigation proved the charge false. The judicial office cited the 《Tang Code》: "One who reports rebellion is not punished in turn."

sentences.zh: 起岩奮謂同列曰：「方今嗣君未立，人情危疑，不亟誅此人，以杜奸謀，慮妨大計。」

translations.literal: Qiyan spoke vigorously to his colleagues: 'At present the successor is not yet established and popular feeling is anxious and doubtful; if we do not quickly execute this man to cut off wicked plotting, I fear it will hinder the great plan.'
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan spoke forcefully to his colleagues: "The heir is not yet enthroned and the people are uneasy. Unless we execute this man at once to cut off conspiracy, I fear the great undertaking will be harmed."

sentences.zh: 趣有司具獄，都人肅然，大事尋定。

translations.literal: He urged the responsible offices to complete the case; the capital people were solemn, and the great affair was soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the authorities to conclude the case. The capital grew calm, and the crisis was soon resolved.

sentences.zh: 中書方列坐銓選，起岩荐一士可用，丞相不悅，起岩即攝衣而起，丞相以為忤己。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat was just sitting in session for selection and appointment; Qiyan recommended a scholar as usable. The chancellor was displeased; Qiyan at once gathered his robes and rose. The chancellor took it as offense against himself.
translations.idiomatic: During a central secretariat session on appointments, Qiyan recommended a capable scholar. The chancellor took offense, and Qiyan immediately gathered his robes and left. The chancellor regarded it as a personal affront.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林侍講學士、知制誥兼修國史，修三朝實錄，加同知經筵事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician Lecturer, Drafter of Proclamations, and concurrent Compiler of National History; he compiled the Veritable Records of three reigns and was given additional charge as Associate Director of the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin academician lecturer, drafter of proclamations, and concurrent national history compiler, edited the veritable records of three reigns, and was given additional charge of the classics mat.

sentences.zh: 御史臺奏除浙西廉訪使，不允。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized to appoint him Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe; it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate recommended him as surveillance commissioner of Western Zhe, but the appointment was denied.

sentences.zh: 已而擢陝西行台侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Attending Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to attending censor on the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 將行，复留為侍講學士。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, he was again retained as Academician Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to leave, he was kept on as academician lecturer.

sentences.zh: 拜江南行台侍御史，召入中台，為侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, summoned into the central censorate, and made Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attending censor on the Jiangnan branch secretariat, then summoned to the central censorate as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 轉燕南廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Yan South.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Yan South.

sentences.zh: 搏擊豪強，不少容貸，貧民賴以吐氣。

translations.literal: He struck at powerful families and showed little indulgence; the poor relied on this to breathe freely.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted the powerful without leniency, and the poor at last had room to breathe.

sentences.zh: 滹沱河水為真定害，起岩論封河神為侯爵，而移文責之，復修其提防，瀹其湮鬱，水患遂息。

translations.literal: The waters of the Hutuo River harmed Zhending; Qiyan argued that enfeoffing the river god as marquis was wrong, and sent an official communication to reprove it; he again repaired the dikes, dredged the choked and stagnant channels, and the flood harm then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Flooding on the Hutuo River was harming Zhending. Qiyan argued that ennobling the river god as a marquis was misguided, sent an official rebuke, repaired the dikes, and dredged the choked channels until the floods subsided.

sentences.zh: 升江南行台御史中丞，拜翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史、知經筵事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief, Drafter of Proclamations, concurrent Compiler of National History, and Director of the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice censor-in-chief on the Jiangnan branch secretariat and was appointed Hanlin expositor-in-chief, drafter of proclamations, concurrent national history compiler, and director of the classics mat.

sentences.zh: 右丞相別裡怯不花為台臣所糾，去位。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Bayinduq Baras Buqa was impeached by the censors and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Bayinduq Baras Buqa was impeached by the censors and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾再入相，諷詞臣言台章之非，起岩執不可，聞者壯之。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the chancellorship again and hinted to the drafting officials that the censors' memorial was wrong; Qiyan held firm that it could not be done, and those who heard were heartened.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned as chancellor and urged the drafting officials to declare the censorial memorial mistaken. Qiyan refused, and those who heard of it took heart.

sentences.zh: 俄拜御史中丞，論事剴直，無所顧忌，與上官多不合。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; in discussing affairs he was incisive and direct, without regard for anything, and often at odds with his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed vice censor-in-chief. His remonstrances were sharp and direct, without fear, and he often clashed with his superiors.

sentences.zh: 詔修遼、金、宋三史，復命入翰林為承旨，充總裁官，積階至榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; he was again ordered into the Hanlin as expositor-in-chief and made Chief Compiler, rising in rank by accumulation to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the compilation of the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, he was again appointed Hanlin expositor-in-chief and chief compiler, eventually rising to grand master for glorious happiness.

sentences.zh: 起岩熟於金源典故，宋儒道學源委，尤多究心，史官有露才自是者，每立言未當，起岩據理竄定，深厚醇雅，理致自足。

translations.literal: Qiyan was well versed in Jin-dynasty precedents and the origins of Song Ru Learning of the Way, and especially devoted study to them. When history officers showed off talent and self-assurance, each time their statements were not right Qiyan corrected them according to reason; his style was deep, thick, pure, and elegant, and the reasoning was sufficient in itself.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan was deeply versed in Jin-dynasty precedents and the origins of Song Neo-Confucian learning. Whenever a history officer paraded his talent and wrote something unsound, Qiyan revised it on principle. His prose was weighty, refined, and lucid in argument.

sentences.zh: 史成，年始六十有五，遂上疏乞骸骨以歸，後四年卒。

translations.literal: When the histories were completed he had just reached sixty-five; he then submitted a memorial begging his old bones to return home, and four years later died.
translations.idiomatic: When the histories were finished he was sixty-five. He submitted a memorial asking to retire, and died four years later.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 起岩面如紫瓊，美髯方頤，而眉目清揚可觀，望而知為雅量君子。

translations.literal: Qiyan's face was like purple jade, with a fine beard and square jaw, yet his brows and eyes were clear and elevated and pleasing to see; at a glance one knew him for a gentleman of generous measure.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan had a face like purple jade, a fine beard, and a square jaw, with clear, spirited brows and eyes. At a glance one could see he was a man of generous character.

sentences.zh: 及其臨政決議，意所背鄉，屹若泰山，不可回奪。

translations.literal: When he faced government and decided policy, whatever direction his mind opposed stood firm as Mount Tai and could not be turned or taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In office, once his mind was set against something, he stood firm as Mount Tai and could not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 或時面折人，面頸發赤，不少恕，廟堂憚之。

translations.literal: At times he would rebuke a man to his face until face and neck flushed red, showing little forgiveness; the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At times he would rebuke someone to his face until his own face and neck flushed with anger, never sparing him, and the court was wary of him.

sentences.zh: 識者謂其外和中剛，不受人籠絡，如歐陽修，名聞四裔。

translations.literal: Those who knew him said that outwardly he was mild and inwardly firm, not subject to others' manipulation, like Ouyang Xiu; his fame reached the four borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew him said he was gentle outwardly and firm within, could not be manipulated, and resembled Ouyang Xiu; his reputation reached the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 安南修貢，其陪臣致其世子之辭，必候起岩起居。

translations.literal: When Annam presented tribute, its attendant ministers, in delivering their heir's message, always waited upon Qiyan's health.
translations.idiomatic: When Annam sent tribute, its attendant ministers always inquired after Qiyan's health before delivering their crown prince's message.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，少處窮約，下帷教授，躬致米百里外，以養父母；

translations.literal: By nature filial and friendly, in youth he lived in poverty and restraint, lowered the curtain to teach, and personally brought rice from a hundred li away to support his parents;
translations.idiomatic: He was filial and devoted to his kin. In youth he lived in poverty, teaching behind closed curtains while personally carrying rice from a hundred li away to support his parents;

sentences.zh: 撫弟如石，教之宦學，無不備至。

translations.literal: he reared his younger brother Rushi, instructing him in official learning, leaving nothing undone.
translations.idiomatic: he raised his younger brother Rushi and guided his education for official service with complete care.

sentences.zh: 舉親族弗克葬者二十餘喪，且買田以給其祭。

translations.literal: He undertook more than twenty burials for kinsmen who could not afford burial, and moreover bought fields to supply their sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged burial for more than twenty kinsmen who could not afford it and bought fields to support their sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 凡獲俸賜，必與故人賓客共之。

translations.literal: Whenever he received salary or gifts he always shared them with old friends and guests.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he received salary or imperial gifts, he shared them with old friends and guests.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，廩無餘粟，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On the day he died the granary had no surplus grain and the household no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his granary held no surplus grain and his household no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 先是，至元乙酉三月乙亥，太史奏文昌星明，文運將興。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the yihai day of the third month of the yiyou year of Zhiyuan, the court astronomer reported that the Wenchang star was bright and the literary fortune would rise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on the yihai day of the third month of the yiyou year of Zhiyuan, the court astronomer reported that the Wenchang star was bright and a literary age was about to dawn.

sentences.zh: 時世祖行幸上京，明日丙子，皇孫降生於儒州。

translations.literal: At that time Shizu was traveling to the Upper Capital; the next day, on the bingzi day, the imperial grandson was born at Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was then traveling to the Upper Capital. The next day, on bingzi, the imperial grandson was born at Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夜，起岩亦生。

translations.literal: That same night Qiyan was also born.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Qiyan was born.

sentences.zh: 其後皇孫踐祚，是為仁宗，始詔設科取士，及廷試，起岩遂為第一人，論者以為非偶然也。

translations.literal: Afterward the imperial grandson ascended the throne—this was Emperor Renzong—who first by edict established the examination to select scholars; at the palace examination Qiyan thus became the first-ranked man. Discussants held this was no accident.
translations.idiomatic: Later that grandson came to the throne as Emperor Renzong and first restored the civil service examinations. At the palace examination Qiyan took first place, which commentators took as no accident.

sentences.zh: 起岩博學有文，善篆、隸，有《華峰漫稿》、《華峰類稿》、《金陵集》各若干卷，藏於家。

translations.literal: Qiyan was broadly learned and possessed of literary talent, skilled in seal and clerical script; he had several juan each of 《Huafeng Casual Drafts》, 《Huafeng Classified Drafts》, and 《Jinling Collection》, kept in his household.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan was broadly learned and a fine writer, skilled in seal and clerical script. His 《Huafeng Casual Drafts》, 《Huafeng Classified Drafts》, and 《Jinling Collection》, each in several juan, were kept at home.

sentences.zh: 子二人：琳，琛。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Lin and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Lin and Chen.

sentences.zh: ○歐陽玄

translations.literal: ○ Ouyang Xuan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ouyang Xuan

sentences.zh: 歐陽玄，字原功，其先家廬陵，與文忠公修同所自出。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xuan, styled Yuangong; his ancestors' household was at Luling, of the same descent as the Cultivated and Loyal Lord Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xuan, whose style was Yuangong, came from a Luling family of the same lineage as Ouyang Xiu, the Cultivated and Loyal Lord.

sentences.zh: 至曾大父新，始遷居瀏陽，故玄為瀏陽人。

translations.literal: By his great-great-grandfather Xin they first moved to settle at Liuyang; therefore Xuan was a man of Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xin was the first to move the family to Liuyang, so Xuan was counted as a native of Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 幼岐嶷，母李氏，親授《孝經》、《論語》、小學諸書，八歲能成誦，始從鄉先生張貫之學，日記數千言，即知屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was precocious; his mother the Lady Li personally taught him the 《Classic of Filial Piety》, the 《Analects》, the Elementary Learning, and other books. At eight he could recite them complete; he then studied under the village teacher Zhang Guan, recording several thousand words a day, and at once knew how to compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was exceptionally bright. His mother Lady Li taught him the 《Classic of Filial Piety》, the 《Analects》, the Elementary Learning, and other texts herself. At eight he could recite them from memory. He then studied under the local teacher Zhang Guan, memorizing several thousand characters a day and learning to write prose almost at once.

sentences.zh: 十歲，有黃冠師注目視玄，謂貫之曰：「是兒神氣凝遠，目光射人，異日當以文章冠世，廊廟之器也。」

translations.literal: At ten, a Daoist master fixed his gaze on Xuan and said to Guan: 'This boy's spirit is concentrated and far-reaching, his eyes shoot forth light; another day he will crown the age with literature—he is material for the court and temple.'
translations.idiomatic: At ten a Daoist priest fixed his gaze on Xuan and told Guan: "This boy's spirit is concentrated and far-seeing, his eyes pierce like light. One day he will lead the world in letters—he is fit for high office."

sentences.zh: 言訖而去，亟追與語，已失所之。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he left; they hurried to pursue and speak with him, but he was already lost to sight.
translations.idiomatic: When he had spoken he left. They hurried after him to talk, but he had vanished.

sentences.zh: 部使者行縣，玄以諸生見，命賦梅花詩，立成十首，晚歸，增至百首，見者駭異之。

translations.literal: A circuit envoy toured the county; Xuan, as a student, was received and ordered to compose poems on plum blossom. He at once completed ten; returning in the evening he increased them to a hundred. Those who saw were startled and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: When a circuit envoy visited the county, Xuan was presented as a student and told to compose poems on plum blossom. He finished ten on the spot and, returning that evening, expanded them to a hundred. All who saw it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 年十四，益從宋故老習為詞章，下筆輒成章，每試庠序，輒佔高等。

translations.literal: At fourteen he further studied literary composition with old Song scholars; when he put pen to paper he at once formed complete pieces. Whenever he was examined at the local school he always took the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he studied literary composition further with old Song scholars. Whatever he wrote came out as finished work, and in every school examination he took the top rank.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，下帷數年，人莫見其面。

translations.literal: At weak crown he lowered the curtain for several years and people did not see his face.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he studied behind closed curtains for several years without showing his face in public.

sentences.zh: 經史百家，靡不研究，伊、洛諸儒源委，尤為淹貫。

translations.literal: The classics, histories, and the hundred schools—none he did not investigate; the origins of the Yi and Luo scholars he was especially thorough in.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics, histories, and the hundred schools without exception and was especially thorough in the origins of the Yi-Luo Neo-Confucians.

sentences.zh: 召為國子博士，升國子監丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Erudite of the National University and promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as an erudite of the National University and promoted to vice director of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 致和元年，遷翰林待制，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe he was transferred to Hanlin Attendant-Drafter and concurrent Compiler of the National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhihe he was made Hanlin attendant-drafter with a concurrent post as national history compiler.

sentences.zh: 時當兵興，玄領印攝院事，日直內廷，參決機務，凡遠近調發，制詔書檄。

translations.literal: At the time warfare was rising; Xuan took the seal and acted in charge of the office's affairs, daily attending in the inner court to participate in deciding secret matters—all distant and near deployments, edicts, proclamations, and dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: War was then breaking out. Xuan took charge of the history office, attended court daily, and helped decide state affairs, drafting all edicts, proclamations, and dispatches for deployments near and far.

sentences.zh: 既而改元天歷，郊廟、建後、立儲、肆赦之文，皆經撰述。

translations.literal: Before long the reign title was changed to Tianli; texts for suburban sacrifice, temple rites, establishing the empress, establishing the heir, and general amnesty—all passed through his drafting.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed to Tianli, he drafted the texts for suburban sacrifice, temple rites, the installation of the empress, the designation of the heir, and the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 复條時政數十事，實封以聞，多推行之。

translations.literal: He again listed several tens of items on current policy, sealed them in substance, and reported them; many were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a sealed memorial listing several dozen policy recommendations, many of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 明年，初置奎章閣學士院，又置藝文監隸焉，皆選清望官居之，文宗親署玄為藝文少監。

translations.literal: The next year the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academician Institute was first established, and the Bureau of Literary Arts was also placed under it; all chose officials of clear reputation to fill the posts. Emperor Wenzong personally signed Xuan as Junior Director of Literary Arts.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Kui Zhang Pavilion academician institute was established, with the Bureau of Literary Arts placed under it, both staffed by officials of high reputation. Emperor Wenzong personally appointed Xuan junior director of literary arts.

sentences.zh: 奉詔纂修《經世大典》，升太監、檢校書籍事。

translations.literal: By imperial order he compiled the 《Comprehensive Statutes for Governing the Age》, was promoted to Senior Director, and made Commissioner for Inspecting Books.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he helped compile the 《Comprehensive Statutes for Governing the Age》, was promoted to senior director, and was made commissioner for inspecting books.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，改僉太常禮儀院事，拜翰林直學士，編修四朝實錄，俄兼國子祭酒，召赴中都議事，升侍講學士，复兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was changed to Associate Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed Hanlin Academician Direct, compiled the Veritable Records of four reigns, and soon was concurrently made Chancellor of the National University; summoned to the Central Capital to discuss affairs, he was promoted to Academician Lecturer and again concurrently Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuantong he became associate administrator of the court of imperial sacrifices and Hanlin academician direct, edited the veritable records of four reigns, and soon added the chancellorship of the National University. Summoned to the central capital for deliberation, he was promoted to academician lecturer while retaining the university chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 重紀至元五年，足患風痺，乞南歸以便醫藥，帝不允。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the renewed Zhizhi era his feet suffered wind paralysis; he begged to return south for convenient medical treatment, and the emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the renewed Zhizhi era his legs were afflicted with paralysis. He asked to return south for medical care, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林學士，未幾，懇辭去位，帝復不允，免其行朝賀禮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician; before long he earnestly begged to leave office. The emperor again did not approve, but exempted him from performing court congratulation rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin academician. Before long he earnestly asked to resign, but the emperor again refused, though he was excused from court congratulation ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 至正改元，更張朝政，事有不便者，集議廷中，玄極言無隱，科目之复，沮者尤眾，玄尤力爭之。

translations.literal: When the reign title was changed to Zhizheng the court government was renewed; matters that were not convenient were gathered for discussion in court. Xuan spoke to the utmost without concealment. On restoring the examination system the obstructors were especially many, and Xuan especially strove for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhizheng era began and the court reorganized government, Xuan spoke frankly in palace deliberations on every difficult issue. The restoration of the civil service examinations met especially strong opposition, and Xuan argued for it with particular force.

sentences.zh: 未幾南歸，復起為翰林學士，以疾未行。

translations.literal: Before long he returned south; he was again raised as Hanlin Academician but because of illness did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned south. He was again appointed Hanlin academician but did not take up the post because of illness.

sentences.zh: 詔修遼、金、宋三史，召為總裁官，發凡舉例，俾論撰者有所據依。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; he was summoned as Chief Compiler, set forth principles and raised examples, so that those who discussed and wrote would have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, he was summoned as chief compiler, laid down principles and examples, and gave the writers a firm basis for their work.

sentences.zh: 史官中有悻悻露才、論議不公者，玄不以口舌爭，俟其呈稿，援筆竄定之，統係自正。

translations.literal: Among the history officers were those resentfully showing off talent whose discussions were not fair; Xuan did not contend with words, but waited until they presented drafts, then took up the brush and revised them—the overall system corrected itself.
translations.idiomatic: Some history officers were resentful show-offs whose judgments were unfair. Xuan did not argue with them in words but waited until they submitted drafts, then revised them himself until the narrative was sound.

sentences.zh: 至於論、贊、表、奏，皆玄屬筆。

translations.literal: As for discussions, encomia, memorial tables, and memorials to the throne—all were entrusted to Xuan's brush.
translations.idiomatic: The discussions, encomia, tables, and memorials were all written by Xuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝以玄歷仕累朝，且有修三史功，諭旨丞相，超授爵秩，遂擬拜翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor, because Xuan had served through successive reigns and moreover had merit in compiling the three histories, instructed the chancellor to grant rank by extraordinary promotion; they then proposed appointing him Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor, noting that Xuan had served through several reigns and had helped compile the three histories, instructed the chancellor to promote him beyond the usual ranks. He was proposed for Hanlin expositor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 及入奏，上稱快者再三。

translations.literal: When he entered to report, the ruler expressed satisfaction again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was reported to the throne, the emperor expressed his pleasure again and again.

sentences.zh: 已而乞致仕，帝復不允。

translations.literal: Before long he begged to retire from office; the emperor again did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to retire, but the emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 御史臺奏除福建廉訪使，行次浙西，疾復作，乃上休致之請，作南山隱居，優游山水之間，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized to appoint him Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian. En route, when he reached Western Zhe, his illness recurred; he then submitted a request for complete retirement, built Southern Mountain Hermitage, wandered freely among mountains and waters, and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate recommended him as surveillance commissioner of Fujian. On the road, when he reached Western Zhe, his illness returned. He submitted a request to retire, built the Southern Mountain Hermitage, and lived at ease among the hills and streams, intending to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 復拜翰林學士承旨，玄屢力辭，不獲命。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief; Xuan repeatedly strove to decline and did not obtain permission.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Hanlin expositor-in-chief, but Xuan repeatedly declined and could not obtain permission.

sentences.zh: 奉敕定國律，尋乞致仕，陳情懇切，乃特授湖廣行中書省右丞致仕，賜白玉束帶，給俸賜以終其身。

translations.literal: By imperial order he fixed the national code; soon he begged to retire from office, stating his case earnestly, and was specially granted retirement as Right Chancellor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, given a white-jade girdle, and provided salary and gifts for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he helped fix the national code. Soon he asked to retire with an earnest memorial and was specially granted retirement as right chancellor of the Huguang branch secretariat, given a white-jade girdle, and provided salary and gifts for life.

sentences.zh: 將行，帝复降旨不允，仍前翰林學士承旨，進階光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, the emperor again sent down an edict not approving, keeping him as before as Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and advancing his rank to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to leave, the emperor again refused and kept him as Hanlin expositor-in-chief, promoting him to grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 十四年，汝潁盜起，蔓延南北，州縣幾無完城。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year bandits rose in Ru and Ying, spreading north and south; prefectures and counties almost had no intact cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year bandits rose in the Ru and Ying region and spread north and south until few prefectures and counties still had intact walls.

sentences.zh: 玄獻招捕之策千餘言，鑿鑿可行，當時不能用。

translations.literal: Xuan presented a strategy for recruitment and suppression of more than a thousand words, solidly feasible, but at the time it could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a plan of more than a thousand words for recruiting loyal forces and suppressing the rebels. It was thoroughly workable, but was not adopted at the time.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，乞致仕，以中原道梗，欲由蜀還鄉，帝復不允。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year he begged to retire; because the roads of the Central Plain were blocked he wished to return home by way of Shu, but the emperor again did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year he asked to retire. With the roads of the central plain blocked, he wished to return home through Shu, but the emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 時將大赦天下，宣赴內府。

translations.literal: At the time a great amnesty for the realm was about to be proclaimed, and he was summoned to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: A great amnesty was about to be proclaimed, and he was summoned to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 玄久病，不能步履，丞相傳旨，肩輿至延春閣下，實異數也。

translations.literal: Xuan had long been ill and could not walk; the chancellor transmitted the order, and he was carried in a sedan chair to below the Yanchun Pavilion—truly an extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had been ill for a long time and could not walk. The chancellor relayed the emperor's order that he be carried in a sedan chair to the Yanchun Pavilion—an extraordinary honor.

sentences.zh: 是歲十二月戊戌，卒於崇教里之寓舍，年八十五。

translations.literal: That year on the wuxu day of the twelfth month he died at his lodging in Chongjiao Lane, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the wuxu day of the twelfth month, he died at his lodging in Chongjiao Lane at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 中書以聞，帝賜賻甚厚，贈崇仁昭德推忠守正功臣、大司徒、柱國，追封楚國公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat reported it; the emperor bestowed funeral gifts in very generous measure, granted the title Meritorious Minister of Honoring Benevolence, Illuminating Virtue, Promoting Loyalty, and Upholding Rectitude, Grand Preceptor, and Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu, and gave the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The central secretariat reported his death. The emperor gave lavish funeral gifts and posthumously honored him as meritorious minister of honoring benevolence, illuminating virtue, promoting loyalty, and upholding rectitude, grand preceptor, and pillar of the state, enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 玄性度雍容，含弘縝密，處己儉約，為政廉平。

translations.literal: Xuan by nature was dignified and easy in bearing, inclusive and broad yet finely exact, frugal in his personal conduct, and fair and incorrupt in administration.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Xuan was dignified and unhurried, broad-minded yet finely exact, frugal in his private life, and upright and even-handed in government.

sentences.zh: 歷官四十餘年，在朝之日，殆四之三。

translations.literal: Over more than forty years in office, the days he spent at court amounted to roughly four parts out of five.
translations.idiomatic: In more than forty years of service, he spent roughly three quarters of his career at court.

sentences.zh: 三任成均，而兩為祭酒，六入翰林，而三拜承旨。

translations.literal: He thrice served at the Directorate of Education and twice was its Libationer; he entered the Hanlin six times and thrice received appointment as Expositor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served three times at the Imperial University, twice as its rector, entered the Hanlin Academy six times, and three times was appointed expositor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 修實錄、《大典》、三史，皆大製作。

translations.literal: Compiling the Veritable Records, the 《Grand Compendium》, and the Three Histories—all were great undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: His work on the Veritable Records, the 《Grand Compendium》, and the Three Histories were all major state projects.

sentences.zh: 屢主文衡，兩知貢舉及讀卷官，凡宗廟朝廷雄文大冊、播告萬方制誥，多出玄手。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presided over literary examinations, twice served as chief examiner and as reader of examination papers; for state documents great and solemn for the ancestral temple and court, and proclamations and edicts broadcast to all quarters, most came from Xuan's hand.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly oversaw the civil examinations and twice served as chief examiner and paper reader. Most of the court's grand ceremonial writings for the ancestral temple and state, and the edicts and proclamations sent throughout the realm, came from Xuan's pen.

sentences.zh: 金繒上尊之賜，幾無虛歲。

translations.literal: Gifts of gold and silk with cups of honor were bestowed almost without a year passing idle.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly every year brought him gifts of gold, silk, and ceremonial wine cups from the throne.

sentences.zh: 海內名山大川，釋、老之宮，王公貴人墓隧之碑，得玄文辭以為榮。

translations.literal: Within the realm, famous mountains and great rivers, temples of Buddhism and Daoism, and tomb steles of princes, dukes, and great nobles—all regarded obtaining Xuan's writing as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Across the empire, whether on famous mountains and rivers, in Buddhist and Daoist shrines, or on the tomb steles of princes and great nobles, to obtain a composition from Xuan was counted an honor.

sentences.zh: 片言隻字，流傳人間，咸知寶重。

translations.literal: Single words and stray characters circulating among people were all known and treasured as precious.
translations.idiomatic: Even a stray line of his writing, passing among ordinary readers, was prized as something rare.

sentences.zh: 文章道德，卓然名世。

translations.literal: In literary talent and moral worth he stood forth and was famed in his age.
translations.idiomatic: In both literary accomplishment and moral stature he stood out as a figure of his age.

sentences.zh: 羽儀斯文，贊衛治具，與有功焉。

translations.literal: With his feathers and regalia he adorned the civil tradition and helped uphold the instruments of good governance; in this he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He adorned the civil tradition and helped uphold the institutions of good government, and in this he earned lasting credit.

sentences.zh: 玄無子，以從子達老後，复先玄卒。

translations.literal: Xuan had no son; he took his nephew Daolao as heir, but Daolao again died before Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had no son and adopted his nephew Daolao as heir, but Daolao died before him.

sentences.zh: 有《圭齋文集》若干卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: There is the 《Guizhai Collected Works》 in several fascicles, handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His 《Guizhai Collected Works》, in several volumes, has been handed down to later generations.

sentences.zh: ○許有壬

translations.literal: ○ Xu Youren
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xu Youren

sentences.zh: 許有壬，字可用，其先世居潁，後徙湯陰。

translations.literal: Xu Youren, styled Keyong, his ancestors first dwelt in Ying and later moved to Tangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youren, styled Keyong, came from a family that originally lived in Ying and later moved to Tangyin.

sentences.zh: 有壬幼穎悟，讀書一目五行，嘗閱衡州《淨居院碑》，文近千言，一覽輒背誦無遺。

translations.literal: Youren from youth was quick and perceptive; when he read he could take in five lines at a glance. Once he read the 《Jingju Monastery Stele》 of Hengzhou, nearly a thousand words; with one reading he could recite it from memory without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Youren was bright from childhood and could read five lines at a glance. Once he looked through the nearly thousand-word 《Jingju Monastery Stele》 from Hengzhou and recited it from memory in full after a single reading.

sentences.zh: 年二十，暢師文薦入翰林，不報，授開寧路學正，升教授，未上，辟山北廉訪司書吏。

translations.literal: At age twenty, Chang Shiwen recommended him for entry into the Hanlin; there was no response. He was appointed Confucian instructor of Kaining Circuit, promoted to professor, but before taking up the post was recruited as a clerk of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty, Chang Shiwen recommended him for the Hanlin Academy, but nothing came of it. He was appointed Confucian instructor for Kaining Circuit and promoted to professor, but before reporting he was recruited as a clerk in the Shanbei surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 擢延祐二年進士第，授同知遼州事。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi list of the second year of Yanyou and appointed Associate Intendant of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed associate intendant of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 會關中有警，鄰州聽民出避，棄孩嬰滿道上，有壬獨率弓箭手，閉城門以守，卒獲無虞。

translations.literal: When an alarm arose in Guanzhong, neighboring prefectures allowed the people to flee for safety, and abandoned infants and babies filled the roads. Youren alone led archers, closed the city gates to hold fast, and in the end remained without mishap.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble broke out in Guanzhong, neighboring prefectures let their people flee, and abandoned children lined the roads. Youren alone led his archers, shut the gates, and held the city until the danger passed without harm.

sentences.zh: 州有追逮，不許胥隸足跡至村疃，唯給信牌，令執裡役者呼之，民安而事集。

translations.literal: When the prefecture had matters of pursuit and arrest, he did not allow clerks and runners' footprints to reach villages and hamlets; he only issued identification tokens and had men on corvée duty summon those wanted, so the people were secure and affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: For arrests in the prefecture he forbade runners from entering villages. He issued official tokens instead and had men on corvée duty summon those wanted. The people were left in peace and business still got done.

sentences.zh: 右族貪虐者懲之，冤獄雖有成案，皆平翻而釋其罪，州遂大治。

translations.literal: He punished grasping and brutal members of great clans; in wrongful cases even when judgments were already settled, he overturned them all and released the convicts, and the prefecture then became greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He punished greedy and cruel men among the great families. Even settled cases of injustice he overturned and released the prisoners, and the prefecture came under firm and fair rule.

sentences.zh: 六年己未，除山北​​廉訪司經歷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the jiwei year, he was appointed Administrator of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, jiwei, he was appointed administrator of the Shanbei surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，遷吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 1 he was transferred to chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉江南行台監察御史，行部廣東，以貪墨劾罷廉訪副使哈只蔡衍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, toured Guangdong on circuit duty, and on grounds of corruption impeached and removed Deputy Surveillance Commissioner Haqai Chaiyan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became investigating censor on the Jiangnan branch secretariat, toured Guangdong, and impeached Deputy Surveillance Commissioner Haqai Chaiyan for corruption, bringing about his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 至江西，會廉訪使苗好謙監焚昏鈔，檢視鈔者日至百餘人，好謙恐其有弊，痛鞭之。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangxi, he encountered Surveillance Commissioner Miao Haoqian supervising the burning of worn-out notes; those examining the notes numbered more than a hundred each day. Haoqian feared there were abuses and had them beaten severely.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he came upon Surveillance Commissioner Miao Haoqian supervising the destruction of worn banknotes. More than a hundred examiners worked each day. Fearing fraud, Haoqian had them whipped savagely.

sentences.zh: 人畏罪，率剔真為偽，以迎其意。

translations.literal: The men, fearing guilt, generally scraped genuine notes into forgeries to meet his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified of punishment, they scraped genuine notes to look like counterfeits in order to please him.

sentences.zh: 筦庫吏而下，榜掠無全膚，迄莫能償。

translations.literal: From the treasury clerks downward, those flogged had no whole skin, and in the end none could make compensation.
translations.idiomatic: From the treasury clerks down, those flogged were left without a patch of whole skin, and in the end none could make good the supposed losses.

sentences.zh: 有壬覆視之，率真物也，遂釋之。

translations.literal: Youren re-examined them; they were all genuine notes, and he then released them.
translations.idiomatic: Youren reviewed the notes himself, found them genuine, and had the men released.

sentences.zh: 凡勢官豪民，人畏之如虎狼者，有壬悉擒治以法，部內肅然。

translations.literal: For all powerful officials and great landowners whom people feared like tigers and wolves, Youren seized and punished them all according to law, and within his jurisdiction order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful officials and predatory magnates whom people feared like wolves, Youren seized and punished to the full extent of the law, and his jurisdiction became orderly.

sentences.zh: 召拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，英宗暴崩於南坡，賊臣鐵失遣使者自上京至，封府庫，收百官印，有壬知事急，即往告御史中丞董守庸，守庸謂宮禁事，非子所當問。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year Emperor Yingzong suddenly died at Nanpo. The rebel minister Tie Shi sent envoys from Shangdu to seal the treasury and collect the seals of the hundred officials. Youren knew affairs were urgent and at once went to inform Censor-in-Chief Dong Shouyong. Shouyong said that palace affairs were not what Youren ought to inquire into.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year Emperor Yingzong died suddenly at Nanpo. The traitor Tie Shi sent envoys from Shangdu to seal the treasuries and seize the official seals. Sensing the urgency, Youren went at once to warn Censor-in-Chief Dong Shouyong, who replied that palace affairs were none of his business.

sentences.zh: 有壬即疏守庸及經歷朵爾只班、監察御史郭也先忽都阿附鐵失之罪以俟。

translations.literal: Youren at once memorialized Shouyong and Administrator Duo'erzhiban and Investigating Censor Guo Yesian Hudu for the crime of attaching themselves to Tie Shi, to await judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Youren immediately memorialized against Shouyong, Administrator Duo'erzhiban, and Investigating Censor Guo Yesian Hudu for siding with Tie Shi, reserving their crimes for later judgment.

sentences.zh: 十月，鐵失伏誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Tie Shi was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Tie Shi was put to death.

sentences.zh: 泰定帝發上都，御史大夫紐澤先還京師，有壬即袖疏上之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiding set out from Shangdu; Grand Censor Niuze returned first to the capital. Youren at once tucked a memorial in his sleeve and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Taiding left Shangdu, Grand Censor Niuze returned first to the capital, and Youren submitted a memorial from his sleeve at once.

sentences.zh: 及帝至，复上章言：「帖木迭兒之子瑣南，與聞大逆，乞賜典刑。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, he again submitted a memorial saying: "Suonan, son of Temuder, took part in the great treason; I beg that he be given lawful execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived, he submitted another memorial: "Suonan, Temuder's son, took part in the great treason. I beg that he be executed according to law.

sentences.zh: 其兄弟勿令出入宮禁。

translations.literal: His brothers must not be allowed to enter and leave the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers should not be allowed to enter or leave the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 中書平章政事王毅、右丞高昉，橫罹奪爵，而四川行省平章政事趙世延，受禍尤慘，皆請雪冤復職。」

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Wang Yi and Right Vice Chancellor Gao Fang of the Central Secretariat were unjustly stripped of rank, while Grand Councillor Zhao Shiyan of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat suffered the bitterest injury; I ask that their wrongs be cleared and their offices restored."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Wang Yi and Right Vice Chancellor Gao Fang of the central secretariat were unjustly stripped of rank, and Grand Councillor Zhao Shiyan of the Sichuan branch secretariat suffered even more harshly. I ask that their names be cleared and their offices restored."

sentences.zh: 繼上正始十事：一曰輔翼太子，宜先訓導；

translations.literal: He then submitted the Ten Items for a Correct Beginning: First, in assisting and guiding the crown prince, instruction should come first;
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted the Ten Items for a Correct Beginning: First, in supporting the crown prince, education should come first;

sentences.zh: 二曰遴選長官，宜先培養；

translations.literal: Second, in selecting chief officials, cultivation should come first;
translations.idiomatic: Second, in choosing chief officials, training should come first;

sentences.zh: 三曰通籍宮禁，宜別貴賤；

translations.literal: Third, in granting registry access to the palace precincts, noble and base should be distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Third, in granting access to the palace precincts, high and low rank should be kept apart;

sentences.zh: 四曰欲謹兵權，宜削兼領；

translations.literal: Fourth, if military authority is to be kept strict, concurrent commands should be reduced;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, to tighten military authority, concurrent commands should be cut back;

sentences.zh: 五曰武備廢弛，宜加修飭；

translations.literal: Fifth, with military preparedness neglected and decayed, it should be restored and strengthened;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, with military readiness in decay, it should be restored and strengthened;

sentences.zh: 六曰賊臣妻妾，宜禁勢官徵索；

translations.literal: Sixth, as to the wives and concubines of rebel ministers, powerful officials should be forbidden to seize them;
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the wives and concubines of rebel ministers should be protected from seizure by powerful officials;

sentences.zh: 七曰前赦權以止變，宜再詔以正名；

translations.literal: Seventh, the earlier amnesty was expedient to stop rebellion; a new edict should set names right;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the earlier amnesty was a stopgap to end the crisis; a new edict should restore proper names and ranks;

sentences.zh: 八曰帖木迭兒諸子，宜籍沒以懲惡；

translations.literal: Eighth, the sons of Temuder should have their property registered and confiscated to punish evil;
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the sons of Temuder should have their property confiscated as punishment for their crimes;

sentences.zh: 九曰考驗經費，以減民賦；

translations.literal: Ninth, examine expenditures to reduce the people's tax burdens;
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, audit state expenditures to lighten the people's tax burdens;

sentences.zh: 十曰撙節浮蠹，以紓國用。

translations.literal: Tenth, restrain wasteful excess to relieve the state's finances.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, cut wasteful spending to ease the strain on state finances.

sentences.zh: 帝多從之。

translations.literal: The emperor largely followed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，初立詹事院，選為中議，改中書左司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding, when the Household of the Heir Apparent was first established, he was selected as Middle Discussion Officer and transferred to Left Section Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 1, when the Household of the Heir Apparent was first established, he was chosen as a middle discussion officer and made left section vice director of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 京畿飢，有壬請賑之。

translations.literal: The capital region was famine-stricken; Youren requested relief for it.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck the capital region, and Youren asked that grain be issued for relief.

sentences.zh: 同列讓曰：「子言固善，其如虧國何！」

translations.literal: His colleagues remonstrated, saying: "Your words are indeed good, but what of harming the state!"
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues objected: "What you say is well enough, but how can we afford to drain the treasury!

sentences.zh: 有壬曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Youren said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Youren replied: "Not at all.

sentences.zh: 民，本也，不虧民，顧豈虧國邪！」

translations.literal: The people are the root; if the people are not harmed, how in turn could the state be harmed!"
translations.idiomatic: The people are the foundation. If the people are not harmed, how can the state be harmed!"

sentences.zh: 卒白於丞相，發糧四十萬斛濟之，民賴以活者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the end he reported it to the chancellor, grain of four hundred thousand hu was issued to relieve them, and very many people lived by relying on it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he persuaded the chancellor to release four hundred thousand hu of grain for relief, and a great many people survived because of it.

sentences.zh: 國學舊法，每以積分次第貢以出官，執政用監丞張起岩議，欲廢之，而以推擇德行為務。

translations.literal: Under the old National University system, men were recommended for office in order according to accumulated points; the chief ministers adopted the proposal of Supervisor Zhang Qiyan to abolish it and instead make selection of moral conduct the task.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old National University system, students were recommended for office in order of accumulated points. The chief ministers, following Supervisor Zhang Qiyan's proposal, wanted to abolish that system and select men on moral conduct alone.

sentences.zh: 有壬折之曰：「積分雖未盡善，然可得博學能文之士，若曰惟德行之擇，其名固佳，恐皆厚貌深情，專意外飾，或懵不能識丁矣。」

translations.literal: Youren refuted it, saying: "Though the point system is not yet perfect, it can still yield broadly learned and literate men. If one says only moral conduct is to be chosen, the name is indeed fine, but I fear one will get thick-faced men of deep deceit who devote themselves to outward show, or dullards who cannot even recognize the character ding."
translations.idiomatic: Youren objected: "The point system is not perfect, but it still yields broadly learned and literate men. Choosing on moral conduct alone sounds admirable, but one may end up with hypocrites skilled only in outward display, or dullards who cannot even read."

sentences.zh: 議久不決。

translations.literal: The debate long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: The debate dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，升右司郎中，其事遂行，已而復寢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he was promoted to Right Section Director; the matter was then carried out, but soon afterward was again shelved.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year he was promoted to right section director. The new policy was briefly adopted, then abandoned again.

sentences.zh: 獲盜例有賞，論者多疑其偽，有淹四十餘年者，群訴於馬首，有壬曰：「盜賊方熾，求疵太甚，緩急何以使人！

translations.literal: By precedent there were rewards for capturing bandits; debaters often suspected fraud, and some cases had dragged on more than forty years. A crowd appealed at his horse's head. Youren said: "Bandits are raging; if one seeks flaws too finely, in urgency or ease how can one employ men!
translations.idiomatic: There were standing rewards for capturing bandits, but many suspected fraud, and some claims had waited more than forty years. A crowd appealed to him on the road. Youren said: "Banditry is raging. If we pick every claim apart, how can we get men to act when we need them!

sentences.zh: 但經部使者覆核者，皆予官。」

translations.literal: So long as cases have been reviewed by the branch secretariat envoy, all are to be granted office."
translations.idiomatic: So long as the branch secretariat envoy has reviewed a case, grant the reward."

sentences.zh: 俄移左司郎中，每遇公議，有壬屢爭事得失，汛掃積滯，幾無留牘。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Section Director; whenever public business was discussed, Youren repeatedly contested the rights and wrongs of affairs, swept away accumulated backlogs, and almost no documents remained pending.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made left section director. In every public deliberation he argued forcefully over policy, cleared away long-standing backlogs, and left almost no papers pending.

sentences.zh: 都事宋本退語人曰：「此貞觀、開元間議事也。」

translations.literal: Director Song Ben withdrew and said to others: "This is deliberation such as in the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras."
translations.idiomatic: Director Song Ben withdrew and told others: "This is deliberation worthy of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras."

sentences.zh: 明年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: The next year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went into mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 天曆三年，擢兩淮都轉運鹽司使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianli he was promoted to Commissioner of the Two Huai Regional Salt Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 3 he was appointed commissioner of the Two Huai regional salt transport commission.

sentences.zh: 先是，鹽法壞，廷議非有壬不能集事，故有是命。

translations.literal: Earlier the salt laws had fallen into disorder; court discussion held that without Youren the task could not be accomplished, and so this appointment was made.
translations.idiomatic: The salt laws had broken down, and the court felt that no one but Youren could set them right, which is why he received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 有壬詢究弊端，立法而通融之，國課遂登。

translations.literal: Youren investigated abuses to the root, established laws and made them flexible in application, and state revenue then rose.
translations.idiomatic: Youren traced the abuses to their roots, drew up new regulations with room for practical adjustment, and state revenue rose.

sentences.zh: 至順二年二月，召參議中書省事，未幾，以丁母憂去。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhishun he was summoned as Participating Secretary of the Central Secretariat; before long he left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhishun 2 he was summoned as participating secretary of the central secretariat, but soon left to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，復以參議召。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was again summoned as participating secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 1 he was again summoned as participating secretary.

sentences.zh: 明年甲戌，拜治書侍御史，轉奎章閣學士院侍書學士，仍治台事。

translations.literal: The next year, jiaxu, he was appointed Secretary Censor and transferred to Academician Secretary of the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy, while still administering censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, jiaxu, he was appointed secretary censor and made academician secretary of the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy while still running censorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 會福達魯花赤完卜，藉丞相勢，宿衛東宮，其行頗淫穢，御史劾之，完卜藏御史大夫家，有壬捕而遣之。

translations.literal: It happened that Qarachu darughachi Wanbu, relying on the chancellor's power, served in the night guard of the Eastern Palace; his conduct was quite licentious. The censors impeached him, and Wanbu hid in the censor-in-chief's house. Youren seized him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Qarachu darughachi Wanbu, relying on the chancellor's backing, served in the Eastern Palace guard. His conduct was grossly licentious. When censors impeached him, he hid in the censor-in-chief's house. Youren seized him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 九月，拜中書參知政事、知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was appointed Vice Chancellor of the Central Secretariat and Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed vice chancellor of the central secretariat and lecturer at the classics colloquium.

sentences.zh: 帝詔群臣議上皇太后尊號為太皇太后，有壬曰：「皇上於皇太后，母子也，若加太皇太后，則為孫矣，非禮也。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers to discuss adding the honorific Grand Empress Dowager to the Empress Dowager. Youren said: "Between the emperor and the empress dowager the relation is mother and son. If Grand Empress Dowager is added, he becomes her grandson, which is not proper ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministers to discuss granting the empress dowager the title Grand Empress Dowager. Youren said: "The emperor and the empress dowager are mother and son. If she becomes Grand Empress Dowager, he becomes her grandson in title, which violates proper ritual."

sentences.zh: 眾弗之從，有壬曰：「今制，封贈祖父母，降於父母一等，蓋推恩之法，近重而遠輕，今尊皇太后為太皇太后，是推而遠之，乃反輕矣，豈所謂尊之者邪！」

translations.literal: The assembly did not follow him. Youren said: "Under present regulations, when ennobling or posthumously honoring grandparents, the rank is one grade lower than that of parents—this is the method of extending favor, near heavy and distant light. Now to honor the empress dowager as grand empress dowager is to extend favor outward and thereby make it lighter; is this what is meant by honoring her!"
translations.idiomatic: The assembly would not listen. Youren said: "Under current law, honors granted to grandparents rank one grade below those granted to parents. Favor is meant to weigh most heavily on those nearest. Making the empress dowager a grand empress dowager pushes the honor outward and actually makes it lighter. Is that what honoring her means!"

sentences.zh: 弗之聽。

translations.literal: They would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: They still would not listen.

sentences.zh: 中書平章政事徹理帖木兒挾私憾，奏罷進士科，有壬廷爭甚苦不能奪，遂稱疾在告，帝強起之，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Cherig Temur, nursing a private grudge, memorialized to abolish the jinshi examination. Youren argued bitterly in court but could not prevail, then claimed illness and requested leave. The emperor forcibly recalled him and appointed him Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Cherig Temur, nursing a private grudge, memorialized to abolish the jinshi examination. Youren fought the proposal fiercely at court but could not prevail, then claimed illness and stayed home. The emperor forced him back to office and appointed him attending censor.

sentences.zh: 會汝寧棒胡反，大臣有忌漢官者，取賊所造旗幟及偽宣敕，班地上，問曰：「此欲何為耶？」

translations.literal: When Bang Hu rebelled at Runing, some ministers who resented Han officials took flags and banners the rebels had made and their forged edicts and commissions, spread them on the ground, and asked: "What were these meant to do?"
translations.idiomatic: When Bang Hu rebelled at Runing, ministers hostile to Han officials spread rebel flags and forged edicts on the floor and asked: "What do you make of these?"

sentences.zh: 意漢官諱言反，將以罪中之。

translations.literal: Their intent was that Han officials would shrink from saying "rebellion" and they could then charge them with guilt.
translations.idiomatic: They hoped Han officials would shrink from calling it rebellion so they could be blamed for it.

sentences.zh: 有壬曰：「此曹建年號，稱李老君太子，部署士卒，以敵官軍，其反狀甚明，尚何言！」

translations.literal: Youren said: "These fellows established a reign title, called themselves crown prince of Old Master Li, deployed soldiers, and fought the official army—the signs of rebellion are very clear; what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Youren said: "They proclaimed a reign title, called themselves crown prince of Old Master Li, deployed troops, and fought the official army. The rebellion is plain enough. What more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 其語遂塞。

translations.literal: Their words were then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That silenced them.

sentences.zh: 廷議欲行古劓法，立行樞密院，禁漢人、南人勿學蒙古、畏吾兒字書，有壬皆爭止之。

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to revive the ancient punishment of mutilation, establish a Mobile Pacification Commission, and forbid Han Chinese and Southerners from studying Mongol and Uyghur writing; Youren argued against and stopped them all.
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed reviving ancient mutilation punishments, establishing a mobile pacification commission, and forbidding Han Chinese and Southerners to study Mongol and Uyghur script. Youren fought each proposal and blocked them.

sentences.zh: 重紀至元初，長蘆韓公溥因家藏兵器，遂起大獄，株連台若省，多以贓敗，獨無有壬名，由是忌者益甚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the renewed Zhizhi era, Han Gongpu of Changlu, because of weapons hidden in his household, triggered a great case that implicated the censorate and secretariat; many were ruined for corruption, but Youren's name alone was not among them, and so those who resented him grew even fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the renewed Zhizhi era, Han Gongpu of Changlu triggered a major case over weapons found in his home. It swept through the censorate and secretariat, and many officials fell on corruption charges, but Youren's name was never implicated, which only sharpened the resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 有壬度不可留，遂歸彰德，已而南游湘、漢間。

translations.literal: Youren judged that he could not remain, returned to Zhangde, and afterward traveled south among the Xiang and Han regions.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he could not remain, Youren returned to Zhangde and later traveled south through the Xiang and Han regions.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，召入中書，仍為參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he was summoned into the Central Secretariat and again made Vice Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 6 he was recalled to the central secretariat as vice chancellor.

sentences.zh: 明年，改元至正，有壬極論帝當親祠太廟，母后虛位，徽政院當罷，改元命相當合為上詔，冗職當沙汰，錢糧當裁節，如此之類，不一而足。

translations.literal: The next year the era name was changed to Zhizheng. Youren argued forcefully that the emperor should personally sacrifice at the ancestral temple, that the empress dowager's seat should not be left vacant, that the Huizheng Office should be abolished, that the edicts for the change of era and appointment of chancellors should be combined into one supreme edict, that redundant offices should be purged, and that money and grain should be cut back—matters of this kind, more than can be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the era name was changed to Zhizheng. Youren argued forcefully that the emperor should sacrifice at the ancestral temple in person, that the empress dowager's seat should not be left vacant, that the Huizheng Office should be abolished, that the change of era and appointment of chancellors should be issued in one supreme edict, that redundant offices should be cut, and that spending on money and grain should be reduced—proposals of this kind, and more besides.

sentences.zh: 人皆韙之。

translations.literal: People all approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone approved of his proposals.

sentences.zh: 轉中書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left vice chancellor of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，囊加慶善八及孛羅帖木兒獻議，開西山金口導渾河，逾京城，達通州，以通漕運。

translations.literal: In the second year, Nanggiyasun Baqu and Bolad Temur submitted a proposal to open Jinkou in the Western Hills and channel the Hun River past the capital to reach Tongzhou, so as to open grain transport by canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Nanggiyasun Baqu and Bolad Temur proposed opening Jinkou in the Western Hills and diverting the Hun River through the capital to Tongzhou to revive canal transport.

sentences.zh: 丞相脫脫主之甚力，有壬曰：「渾河之水，湍悍易決，而足以為害，淤淺易塞，而不可行舟；

translations.literal: Chancellor Toqto'a supported it with great force. Youren said: "The waters of the Hun River are swift and fierce and break their banks easily, sufficient to do harm; they silt shallow and block easily and cannot carry boats;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Toqto'a pushed the plan hard. Youren said: "The Hun River runs swift and fierce, breaks its banks easily, and can do great harm. It silts up quickly, blocks easily, and cannot carry boats;

sentences.zh: 況地勢高下，甚有不同，徒勞民費財耳。」

translations.literal: moreover the terrain rises and falls with great difference; it would only waste the people's labor and the state's wealth."
translations.idiomatic: moreover the terrain rises and falls too sharply. It would only waste labor and money."

sentences.zh: 不聽，後卒如有壬言。

translations.literal: They would not listen; afterward events in the end proved as Youren had said.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen, and events later proved him right.

sentences.zh: 先是，有壬之父熙載仕長沙日，設義學，訓諸生。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Youren's father Xizai served at Changsha, he established a charity school to instruct students.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Youren's father Xizai was serving at Changsha, he founded a charity school to instruct students.

sentences.zh: 既歿，而諸生思之，為立東岡書院，朝廷賜額設官，以為育才之地。

translations.literal: After he died, the students missed him and established the Donggang Academy for him; the court granted a plaque and appointed officials, making it a place to nurture talent.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the students missed him and founded the Donggang Academy in his memory. The court granted a plaque, appointed officials, and made it a place to train talent.

sentences.zh: 南台監察御史木八剌沙，緣睚眥怨，言書院不當立，並構浮辭，誣衊有壬，併其二弟有儀、有孚，有壬遂稱病歸。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Mubarak Shah of the Southern Branch Secretariat, on a grudge over a trifle, said the academy ought not to have been established and moreover fabricated loose charges to slander Youren, together with his two younger brothers Youyi and Youfu. Youren then claimed illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Mubarak Shah, investigating censor on the southern branch secretariat, nursed a petty grudge and argued that the academy should never have been founded. He fabricated slander against Youren and his younger brothers Youyi and Youfu. Youren then claimed illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 四年，改江浙行省左丞，辭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Left Vice Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed left vice chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat and declined.

sentences.zh: 六年，召為翰林學士，既上，又辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Hanlin Academician; after reporting, he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was summoned as Hanlin academician, reported for duty, and declined again.

sentences.zh: 監察御史累章辨其誣。

translations.literal: Investigating censors repeatedly submitted memorials clearing the slander.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censors repeatedly memorialized to clear the slander against him.

sentences.zh: 俄拜浙西廉訪使，未上，復以翰林學士承旨召，仍知經筵事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe; before reporting, he was again summoned as Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and still directed the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Western Zhe, but before reporting he was again summoned as Hanlin expositor-in-chief and still directed the classics colloquium.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，授御史中丞，賜白玉束帶及御衣一襲，未幾，復以病歸。

translations.literal: The next summer he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and granted a white-jade girdle and one suit of imperial robes; before long he again returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer he was appointed vice censor-in-chief and given a white-jade girdle and a suit of imperial robes. Before long he again went home, claiming illness.

sentences.zh: 監察御史答蘭不花銜有壬，時短長之，奏劾甚力，事尋白。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Dalan Buqa bore a grudge against Youren and at times spoke of his faults and merits; he memorialized to impeach with great force, but the matter was soon cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Dalan Buqa resented Youren and often spoke of his faults. He impeached him vigorously, but the charges were soon cleared.

sentences.zh: 十二年，盜起河南，聲撼河朔間，有壬畫備御之策十五條，以授郡將，民藉以安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year bandits rose in Henan, their clamor shaking the region between the Yellow River and the northern frontier. Youren drafted fifteen items of defense and preparedness and gave them to the prefectural commanders; the people relied on them and were secure.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year bandits rose in Henan, their threat shaking the lands between the Yellow River and the northern frontier. Youren drafted fifteen measures for defense and preparedness and gave them to the local commanders, and the people were kept safe.

sentences.zh: 十三年，起拜河南行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was recalled and appointed Left Vice Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
