translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was recalled and appointed left vice chancellor of the Henan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣將出征，環河南境，連營以百數，一切芻餉，皆仰給之，有壬從容集事，若平時然。

translations.literal: The court sent generals on campaign; encircling the Henan frontier, linked camps numbered in the hundreds. All fodder and provisions depended on supply from there. Youren calmly gathered affairs together as if in normal times.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent generals on campaign. Around the Henan frontier, camps linked in the hundreds, and all fodder and provisions depended on supplies from Youren's province. He calmly kept affairs in order as if it were peacetime.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷集賢大學士，尋改樞密副使，復拜中書左丞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, soon changed to Vice Director of the Military Affairs Commission, and again appointed Left Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, soon transferred to vice director of the Military Affairs Commission, and again appointed left vice chancellor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時以言為諱，有壬力言朝廷務行姑息之政，賞重罰輕，故將士貪掠子女玉帛而無鬥志，遂倡招降之策，言多不載。

translations.literal: At the time speech was taboo. Youren forcefully said the court pursued a policy of indulgence—rewards heavy and punishments light—so officers and soldiers plundered women, children, jade, and silk without fighting spirit. He then advocated a policy of accepting surrenders; much of what he said was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Speech was dangerous at the time, yet Youren spoke bluntly: the court pursued indulgence, rewarding heavily and punishing lightly, so soldiers plundered women, children, jade, and silk without any will to fight. He then urged a policy of accepting surrenders, though much of what he said went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 有僧名開，自高郵來，言張士誠乞降，眾幸事且成，皆大喜，有壬獨疑其妄，呼僧詰之，果語塞不能對。

translations.literal: There was a monk named Kai who came from Gaoyou and said Zhang Shicheng begged to surrender. Everyone hoped the matter would succeed and all rejoiced greatly. Youren alone suspected it was false, summoned the monk to question him, and indeed he was speechless and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Kai came from Gaoyou claiming that Zhang Shicheng wished to surrender. Everyone hoped the war might end and rejoiced, but Youren alone doubted the story. He summoned the monk and questioned him; the man was speechless and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 轉集賢大學士，兼太子左諭德，階至光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and his rank reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and concurrently left mentor to the heir apparent, rising to grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 有壬前朝舊德，太子頗敬禮之。

translations.literal: Youren was an elder of merit from the previous reign, and the heir apparent treated him with considerable respect.
translations.idiomatic: Youren was a veteran minister of the previous reign, and the heir apparent treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 一日入見，方臂鷙禽以為樂，遽呼左右屏去。

translations.literal: One day when Youren entered for an audience, the heir was just amusing himself with a fierce hawk on his arm and hurriedly ordered his attendants to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: One day when Youren came for an audience, the heir was amusing himself with a fierce hawk on his arm and hurriedly ordered his attendants to take it away.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以老病，力乞致其事，久之始得請，給俸賜以終其身。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, on grounds of old age and illness, he forcefully begged to retire from office. Only after a long time was his request granted, and he was given salary and gifts for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, citing old age and illness, he repeatedly begged to retire. Only after a long delay was he permitted to withdraw, with salary and gifts granted for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 二十四年九月二十一日卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year he died, at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 有壬歷事七朝，垂五十年，遇國家大事，無不盡言，皆一根至理，而曲盡人情。

translations.literal: Youren served through seven reigns for nearly fifty years. Whenever the state faced great affairs, he spoke out without reserve. All his words were rooted in principle and fully measured human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Youren served seven reigns for nearly fifty years. Whenever the state faced a great crisis, he spoke without reserve, always grounding his words in principle and weighing them against human feeling.

sentences.zh: 當權臣恣睢之時，稍忤意，輒誅竄隨之，有壬絕不為巧避計，事有不便，明辨力諍，不知有死生利害，君子多之。

translations.literal: When powerful ministers ran rampant, the slightest offense brought execution or banishment in its wake. Youren never resorted to artful evasion. When something was inconvenient, he argued clearly and remonstrated forcefully, heedless of life, death, gain, or harm. Men of integrity praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful ministers ran rampant, the slightest offense could bring execution or banishment. Youren never tried to evade them by clever means. When policy went wrong, he argued clearly and remonstrated forcefully, heedless of life, death, gain, or harm. Men of integrity praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 有壬善筆札，工辭章，歐陽玄序其文，謂其雄渾閎雋，湧如層瀾，迫而求之，則淵靚深實，蓋深許之也。

translations.literal: Youren was skilled at calligraphy and letters and adept at literary composition. Ouyang Xuan prefaced his writings, saying they were grand, vast, and lofty, surging like layered waves; pressed further, they proved deep, clear, and solid. He clearly thought highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Youren was skilled in calligraphy and letters and excelled at literary composition. Ouyang Xuan prefaced his writings, calling them grand and lofty, surging like layered waves; pressed further, they proved deep, clear, and solid. He clearly thought very highly of him.

sentences.zh: 所著有《至正集》若干卷。

translations.literal: His writings include the 《Collected Works of the Zhizheng Era》 in several fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include the 《Collected Works of the Zhizheng Era》 in several fascicles.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文忠。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Cultured and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Cultured and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子一人，曰禎。

translations.literal: He had one son, named Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son, named Zhen.

sentences.zh: ○宋本

translations.literal: ○ Song Ben
translations.idiomatic: ○ Song Ben

sentences.zh: 宋本，字誠夫，大都人。

translations.literal: Song Ben, styled Chengfu, was a man of Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ben, styled Chengfu, was a native of Dadu.

sentences.zh: 自幼穎拔異群兒，既成童，聚經史窮日夜讀之，句探字索，必通貫乃已。

translations.literal: From childhood he was sharp and stood out among other boys. Once he reached maturity, he gathered the classics and histories and read them day and night, probing every phrase and searching every character until he had mastered them through and through.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was unusually bright among his peers. Once he came of age, he gathered the classics and histories and read them day and night, probing every phrase and searching every character until he had mastered them completely.

sentences.zh: 嘗從父禎官江陵，​​江陵王奎文，明性命義理之學，本往質所得，造詣日深。

translations.literal: He once followed his father Zhen to an office at Jiangling. Wang Kuiwen of Jiangling was versed in the learning of human nature and moral principle. Ben went to him to inquire into what he had gained, and his attainment grew deeper day by day.
translations.idiomatic: He once followed his father Zhen to an appointment at Jiangling. Wang Kuiwen of Jiangling was versed in the learning of human nature and moral principle. Ben went to him to test what he had learned, and his understanding grew deeper day by day.

sentences.zh: 善為古文，辭必己出，峻潔刻厲，多微辭。

translations.literal: He was skilled at ancient-style prose. His language was always his own—severe, pure, incisive, and often laden with subtle meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at ancient-style prose. His language was always his own—severe, pure, and incisive, often laden with subtle meaning.

sentences.zh: 年四十，始還燕。

translations.literal: At forty he returned to Yan for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he returned to Yan for the first time.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，策天下士於廷，本為第一人，賜進士及第，授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhizhi reign, the court examined scholars throughout the realm. Ben ranked first, was granted jinshi with honors, and appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhizhi reign, the court examined scholars throughout the realm. Ben ranked first, received jinshi with honors, and was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年春，除監察御史，首言：「逆賊鐵失等雖伏誅，其黨樞密副使阿散，身親弒逆，以告變得不死，竄嶺南，乞早正天討。」

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of the Taiding reign he was appointed investigating censor. First he said: "The rebel Tieshi and others, though executed, their clique—the Vice Director of Military Affairs Asan—personally took part in regicide, yet by reporting the plot escaped death and was banished to Lingnan. I beg that heavenly punishment be promptly carried out."
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of the Taiding reign he was appointed investigating censor. First he said: "The rebel Tieshi and others, though executed, their clique—the vice director of military affairs Asan—personally took part in regicide, yet by reporting the plot escaped death and was banished to Lingnan. I beg that heavenly punishment be promptly carried out."

sentences.zh: 國製，範黃金為太廟神主，仁宗室盜竟竊去，本言：「在法，民間失盜，捕之違期不獲猶治罪，太常失典守，及在京應捕官，皆當罷去。」

translations.literal: By national institution, spirit tablets for the ancestral temple were cast in pure gold; the tablet from Renzong's chamber was actually stolen. Ben said: "By law, when common people lose goods to theft, failure to capture the thief within the deadline still incurs punishment. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices failed in custodial duty, and the Beijing arrest officers all ought to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: By national institution, spirit tablets for the ancestral temple were cast in pure gold, yet the tablet from Renzong's chamber was actually stolen. Ben said: "By law, when common people lose goods to theft, failure to capture the thief within the deadline still incurs punishment. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices failed in custodial duty, and the Beijing arrest officers all ought to be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 又言：「中書宰執，日趨禁中，固寵苟安，兼旬不至中堂，壅滯機務，乞戒飭臣僚，自非入宿衛日，必詣所署治事。」

translations.literal: Furthermore he said: "The chancellors of the Secretariat daily rush to the inner palace, clinging to favor and settling for safety. For ten days or more they do not come to the main hall, obstructing urgent business. I beg that officials be warned: except on days of palace guard duty, they must go to their offices to conduct affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore he said: "The chancellors of the Secretariat daily rush to the inner palace, clinging to favor and settling for safety. For ten days or more they do not come to the main hall, obstructing urgent business. I beg that officials be warned: except on days of palace guard duty, they must go to their offices to conduct affairs."

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None of these received response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these received response.

sentences.zh: 踰月，調國子監丞。

translations.literal: After a month he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he was transferred to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 夏，風烈地震，有旨集百官雜議弭災之道。

translations.literal: In summer fierce winds and an earthquake struck. An edict ordered officials gathered to discuss various means of quelling the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In summer fierce winds and an earthquake struck. An edict ordered officials gathered to discuss various means of quelling the disaster.

sentences.zh: 時宿衛士自北方來者，復遣歸，乃百十為群，剽劫殺人桓州道中。

translations.literal: At the time palace guards who had come from the north were being sent home again. They banded together in groups of a hundred or ten and robbed and killed people on the road to Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time palace guards who had come from the north were being sent home again. They banded together in groups of a hundred or ten and robbed and killed people on the road to Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 既逮捕，旭滅傑奏釋之。

translations.literal: After they were arrested, Xumiejie memorialized to release them.
translations.idiomatic: After they were arrested, Xumiejie memorialized to have them released.

sentences.zh: 蒙古千戶使京師​​，宿邸中，適民間硃甲妻女車過邸門，千戶悅之，並從者奪以入，硃泣訴於中書，旭滅傑庇不問。

translations.literal: A Mongol chiliarch was sent to the capital and lodged at an inn. Just then a commoner's wife and daughter in a Zhu-family carriage passed the inn gate. The chiliarch took a liking to them, and together with his followers seized them and carried them inside. Zhu wept and appealed to the Secretariat, but Xumiejie shielded the offenders and would not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: A Mongol chiliarch was sent to the capital and lodged at an inn. Just then the wife and daughter of a man surnamed Zhu passed the inn gate in a carriage. The chiliarch took a liking to them, and together with his followers seized them and carried them inside. Zhu wept and appealed to the Secretariat, but Xumiejie shielded the offenders and would not inquire.

sentences.zh: 本適與議，本復抗言：「鐵失餘黨未誅，仁廟神主盜未得，桓州盜未治，硃甲冤未伸，刑政失度，民憤天怨，災異之見，職此之由。」

translations.literal: Ben happened to be present at the deliberation and again spoke out forcefully: "Tieshi's remaining clique has not been executed, the thief of Renzong's spirit tablet has not been captured, the Huanzhou bandits have not been punished, Zhu's grievance has not been redressed, criminal administration has lost its measure, the people are angry and Heaven is resentful—the appearance of portents and disasters arises from this."
translations.idiomatic: Ben happened to be present at the deliberation and again spoke out forcefully: "Tieshi's remaining clique has not been executed, the thief of Renzong's spirit tablet has not been captured, the Huanzhou bandits have not been punished, Zhu's grievance has not been redressed, criminal administration has lost its measure, the people are angry and Heaven is resentful—the appearance of portents and disasters arises from this."

sentences.zh: 辭氣激奮，眾皆聳聽。

translations.literal: His words were fierce and impassioned, and all present listened in awe.
translations.idiomatic: His words were fierce and impassioned, and all present listened in awe.

sentences.zh: 冬，移兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In winter he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉中書左司都事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Director of the Left Department of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to director of the left department of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會議招撫溪洞民，故將李牢山之子嘗假兵部尚書，從諸王帥兵徵鬱林州徭民，李在道納妾，留不進，兵敗歸，樞密副使王卜鄰吉台言：「李平徭有功，當遷官。」

translations.literal: At a conference on pacifying the stream-cave people, the son of the former general Li Laoshan had once borrowed the title Minister of War and followed a prince in leading troops to campaign against the Yao people of Yulin Prefecture. Li took a concubine on the march, halted and would not advance, returned after defeat, and Vice Director of Military Affairs Wang Buling said at the Secretariat: "Li pacified the Yao with merit and ought to be promoted."
translations.idiomatic: At a conference on pacifying the stream-cave people, the son of the former general Li Laoshan had once borrowed the title minister of war and followed a prince in leading troops against the Yao people of Yulin Prefecture. Li took a concubine on the march, halted and would not advance, and returned after defeat. Vice director of military affairs Wang Buling said at the Secretariat: "Li pacified the Yao with merit and ought to be promoted."

sentences.zh: 本言；

translations.literal: Ben said;
translations.idiomatic: Ben said;

sentences.zh: 「李棄軍娶妾，逗撓軍期，宜亟置諸法，況可官邪！」

translations.literal: "Li abandoned the army to take a concubine and delayed the campaign schedule. He ought swiftly to be punished by law—how much less ought he be given office!"
translations.idiomatic: "Li abandoned the army to take a concubine and delayed the campaign schedule. He ought swiftly to be punished by law—how much less ought he be given office!"

sentences.zh: 王色沮，乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Wang's color fell, and he no longer dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wang's color fell, and he no longer dared speak.

sentences.zh: 旭滅傑死，左丞相倒剌沙當國得君，與平章政事烏伯都剌，皆西域人，西域富賈以其國異石名曰瓓者來獻，其估巨萬，或未酬其直；

translations.literal: When Xumiejie died, Left Chancellor Daula Shah held state power and won the emperor's trust, together with Central Chancellor Ubaidullah—both were men of the Western Regions. A wealthy merchant of the Western Regions brought as tribute a strange stone from his country called Lan, valued at tens of thousands, yet its price was sometimes unpaid;
translations.idiomatic: When Xumiejie died, left chancellor Daula Shah held state power and won the emperor's trust, together with central chancellor Ubaidullah—both were men of the Western Regions. A wealthy merchant of the Western Regions brought as tribute a strange stone from his country called Lan, valued at tens of thousands, yet its price was sometimes unpaid;

sentences.zh: 諸嘗有過，為司憲褫官，或有出其門下者。

translations.literal: some who had once been at fault and were stripped of office by the censorate, or some who had come from their households.
translations.idiomatic: some who had once been at fault and were stripped of office by the censorate, or some who had come from their households.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，烏伯都剌自禁中出，至政事堂，集宰執僚佐，命左司員外郎胡彝以詔稿示本，乃以星孛地震赦天下，仍命中書酬累朝所獻諸物之直，擢用自英廟至今為憲台奪官者。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year Ubaidullah came out from the inner palace to the Hall of Administration, gathered the chancellors and their staff, and ordered Left Department Vice Director Hu Yi to show Ben the draft edict. It was to pardon the realm on account of a comet and earthquake, still order the Secretariat to pay the prices of objects presented by successive reigns, and promote those stripped of office by the censorate from Emperor Yingzong's reign to the present.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the third year Ubaidullah came out from the inner palace to the Hall of Administration, gathered the chancellors and their staff, and ordered left department vice director Hu Yi to show Ben the draft edict. It was to pardon the realm on account of a comet and earthquake, still order the Secretariat to pay the prices of objects presented by successive reigns, and promote those stripped of office by the censorate from Emperor Yingzong's reign to the present.

sentences.zh: 本讀竟，白曰：「今警災異，而畏獻物未酬直者憤怨，此有司細故，形諸王言，必貽笑天下。

translations.literal: When Ben had finished reading, he reported: "Now we warn of portents and disasters, yet we fear the anger and resentment of those whose tribute objects have not been paid for. These are petty matters for the offices. To put them in an imperial edict will surely make the realm laugh.
translations.idiomatic: When Ben had finished reading, he reported: "Now we warn of portents and disasters, yet we fear the anger and resentment of those whose tribute objects have not been paid for. These are petty matters for the offices. To put them in an imperial edict will surely make the realm laugh.

sentences.zh: 司憲褫有罪者官，世祖成憲也，今上即位，累詔法世祖，今擢用之，是廢成憲而反汗前詔也，後復有邪佞贓穢者，將治之邪？

translations.literal: The censorate stripped office from the guilty according to the established statutes of Emperor Shizu. Since the present emperor ascended the throne, repeated edicts have ordered that law follow Shizu. Now to promote and employ them is to abolish the established statutes and go back on earlier edicts. Later, when wicked and corrupt men appear again, will you punish them?
translations.idiomatic: The censorate stripped office from the guilty according to the established statutes of Emperor Shizu. Since the present emperor ascended the throne, repeated edicts have ordered that law follow Shizu. Now to promote and employ them is to abolish the established statutes and go back on earlier edicts. Later, when wicked and corrupt men appear again, will you punish them?

sentences.zh: 置不問邪？」

translations.literal: Or leave them unpunished?"
translations.idiomatic: Or leave them unpunished?"

sentences.zh: 宰執聞本言，相視嘆息罷去。

translations.literal: When the chancellors heard Ben's words, they looked at one another, sighed, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the chancellors heard Ben's words, they looked at one another, sighed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日，宣詔竟，本遂稱疾不出。

translations.literal: The next day, after the edict was fully promulgated, Ben then claimed illness and did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, after the edict was fully promulgated, Ben then claimed illness and did not appear.

sentences.zh: 四年春，遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year he was transferred to director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年冬，升吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In winter of the first year of the Tianli reign he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the first year of the Tianli reign he was promoted to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was changed to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 是年，文宗開奎章閣，置藝文監，檢校書籍，超大監。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Wenzong opened the Kuizhang Pavilion, established the Directorate of Literary Arts to inspect books, and Ben was promoted above director.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Wenzong opened the Kuizhang Pavilion, established the Directorate of Literary Arts to inspect books, and Ben was promoted above director.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，進奎章閣學士院供奉學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhishun reign he was promoted to Academician Attendant of the Kuizhang Pavilion Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhishun reign he was promoted to academician attendant of the Kuizhang Pavilion Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，出為河東廉訪副使，將行，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year he was sent out as Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Hedong. Just as he was about to depart, he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the second year he was sent out as vice surveillance commissioner of Hedong. Just as he was about to depart, he was promoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，寧宗崩，順帝未至，皇太后在興聖宮，正旦，議循故事，行朝賀禮，本言：「宜上表興聖宮，廢大明殿朝賀。」

translations.literal: In winter of the third year Emperor Ningzong died and Emperor Shundi had not yet arrived. The empress dowager was at Xingsheng Palace. At New Year's Day, following precedent, they deliberated on performing the court congratulation rites. Ben said: "It is fitting to submit a memorial at Xingsheng Palace and abolish the court congratulation at the Daming Hall."
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the third year Emperor Ningzong died and Emperor Shundi had not yet arrived. The empress dowager was at Xingsheng Palace. At New Year's Day, following precedent, they deliberated on performing the court congratulation rites. Ben said: "It is fitting to submit a memorial at Xingsheng Palace and abolish the court congratulation at the Daming Hall."

sentences.zh: 眾是而從之。

translations.literal: The assembly agreed and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly agreed and followed him.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，兼經筵官，冬，拜陝西行台治書侍御史，不拜，复留為奎章閣學士院承製學士，仍兼經筵官。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Yuantong reign he concurrently served as classics colloquium official. In winter he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat but did not accept. He was again retained as Drafting Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion Academy and still concurrently served as classics colloquium official.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuantong reign he concurrently served as classics colloquium official. In winter he was appointed investigating censor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat but did not accept. He was again retained as drafting academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion Academy and still concurrently served as classics colloquium official.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，轉集賢直學士，兼國子祭酒，兼經筵如故。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year he was transferred to Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and his classics colloquium duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the second year he was transferred to direct academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and his classics colloquium duties remained as before.

sentences.zh: 是年冬十一月二十五日卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: That year, on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month, he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month, he died, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 階官自承務郎十轉至太中大夫。

translations.literal: His rank in office rose through ten steps from Gentleman for Court Service to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His rank in office rose through ten steps from gentleman for court service to grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 本性高抗不屈，持論堅正，制行純白，不可干以私，而篤朋友之義，堅若金鐵，人有片善，稱道不少置，尤以植立斯文自任。

translations.literal: By nature Ben was lofty and unyielding. He held to upright principles, conducted himself in pure integrity, and could not be swayed by private interest. Yet he was devoted to the duty of friendship, firm as gold and iron. If a man had even a small virtue, he praised it without stint. Above all he took upon himself the task of upholding civilization.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Ben was lofty and unyielding. He held to upright principles, conducted himself with pure integrity, and could not be swayed by private interest. Yet he was devoted to the duty of friendship, firm as gold and iron. If a man had even a small virtue, he praised it without stint. Above all he took upon himself the task of upholding civilization.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉，取進士滿百人額；

translations.literal: When he supervised the examinations, he filled the quota of one hundred jinshi;
translations.idiomatic: When he supervised the examinations, he filled the quota of one hundred jinshi;

sentences.zh: 為讀卷官，增第一甲為三人。

translations.literal: as reading examiner he increased the first class to three men.
translations.idiomatic: as reading examiner he increased the first class to three men.

sentences.zh: 父官南中，貧，賣宅以去，

translations.literal: When his father served in the south, they were poor and sold the house to depart.
translations.idiomatic: When his father served in the south, they were poor and sold the house to depart.

sentences.zh: 居官清慎自持，饘粥至不給。

translations.literal: Ben, in office, maintained pure caution in self-conduct, sometimes scarcely having enough porridge.
translations.idiomatic: Ben, in office, maintained pure caution in self-conduct, sometimes scarcely having enough porridge.

sentences.zh: 本未弱冠，聚徒以養親，殆二十年，歷仕通顯，猶僦屋以居。

translations.literal: Before Ben had reached twenty, he gathered students to support his parents, for nearly twenty years. Though he rose through office to eminence, he still rented a house to live in.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ben had reached twenty, he gathered students to support his parents, for nearly twenty years. Though he rose through office to eminence, he still rented a house to live in.

sentences.zh: 及卒，非賻贈幾不能給棺斂，執紼者近二千人，皆縉紳大夫、門生故吏及國子諸生，未嘗有一雜賓，時人榮之。

translations.literal: When he died, but for funeral gifts he could scarcely have afforded coffin and burial. Nearly two thousand men carried the mourning cord— all gentry officials, students, former subordinates, and students of the Directorate of Education. Never was there a single miscellaneous guest. People of the time honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, but for funeral gifts he could scarcely have afforded coffin and burial. Nearly two thousand men carried the mourning cord—all gentry officials, students, former subordinates, and students of the Directorate of Education. Never was there a single miscellaneous guest. People of the time honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 本所著有《至治集》四十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Ben's writings include the 《Collected Works of the Zhizhi Reign》 in forty fascicles, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Ben's writings include the 《Collected Works of the Zhizhi Reign》 in forty fascicles, circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 諡正獻。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Upright Presentation.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Upright Presentation.

sentences.zh: ○謝端

translations.literal: ○ Xie Duan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xie Duan

sentences.zh: 謝端，字敬德，蜀之遂寧人。

translations.literal: Xie Duan, styled Jingde, was a man of Suining in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Duan, styled Jingde, was a native of Suining in Shu.

sentences.zh: 宋末，蜀士多避兵江陵，因家焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Song, many scholars of Shu fled the warfare to Jiangling and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Song, many scholars of Shu fled the warfare to Jiangling and settled there.

sentences.zh: 端幼穎異，五六歲能吟詩，十歲能作賦。

translations.literal: Duan was precocious from childhood. At five or six he could recite poetry; at ten he could compose fu.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was precocious from childhood. At five or six he could recite poetry; at ten he could compose fu.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，與尚書宋本同師，明性理，為古文，又同教授江陵城中，以文學齊名，時號「謝宋」。

translations.literal: At twenty he studied under the same teacher as Minister Song Ben, mastered moral principle, wrote ancient-style prose, and together taught in Jiangling city. They were equally famed in letters, and people of the time called them "Xie and Song."
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he studied under the same teacher as Minister Song Ben, mastered moral principle, wrote ancient-style prose, and together they taught in Jiangling city. They were equally famed in letters, and people of the time called them "Xie and Song."

sentences.zh: 史槓宣慰荊南，數加延禮，薦之姚燧，燧方以文章大名自負，少所許可，以所為文眎端，端一讀，即能指擿其用意所在，燧嘆獎不已，語人：「後二十年，若謝端者，豈易得哉！」

translations.literal: Shi Geng, pacification commissioner of Jingnan, repeatedly extended him courtesy and recommended him to Yao Sui. Yao Sui, then proud of his great name in letters, seldom approved others. He showed Duan what he had written. Duan read it once and could point out where his meaning lay. Yao Sui sighed in admiration without end and told others: "Twenty years from now, will a man like Xie Duan be easy to find!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Geng, pacification commissioner of Jingnan, repeatedly extended him courtesy and recommended him to Yao Sui. Yao Sui, then proud of his great name in letters, seldom approved others. He showed Duan what he had written. Duan read it once and could point out where his meaning lay. Yao Sui sighed in admiration without end and told others: "Twenty years from now, will a man like Xie Duan be easy to find!"

sentences.zh: 用薦者署校官，不報。

translations.literal: Through the recommender he was appointed a school official, but no response came.
translations.idiomatic: Through the recommender he was appointed a school official, but no response came.

sentences.zh: 科舉法行，就試河南行省，中其舉，以內艱不會試。

translations.literal: When the examination system was implemented, he took the test at the Henan Branch Secretariat and passed its examination, but because of mourning for his mother did not attend the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: When the examination system was implemented, he took the test at the Henan branch secretariat and passed its examination, but because of mourning for his mother did not attend the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，乃擢進士乙科。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Yanyou reign he was finally selected as jinshi in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yanyou reign he was finally selected as jinshi in the second class.

sentences.zh: 授承事郎、潭州路同知湘陰州事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman for Court Service and Vice Prefect of Xiangyin Prefecture on the Tanzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed gentleman for court service and vice prefect of Xiangyin Prefecture on the Tanzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，入為國子博士，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: When his term ended he entered service as Doctor of the Directorate of Education, then was transferred to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he entered service as doctor of the Directorate of Education, then was transferred to doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 盜入太廟，失第八室黃金主，坐罷去。

translations.literal: Thieves entered the ancestral temple and the golden spirit tablet of the eighth chamber was lost. He was dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves entered the ancestral temple and the golden spirit tablet of the eighth chamber was lost. He was dismissed on that account.

sentences.zh: 端禮官，非典守，不當坐，亦不辨。

translations.literal: Duan was a ritual official, not a custodian by statute, and ought not to have been punished. Yet he did not argue the point.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was a ritual official, not a custodian by statute, and ought not to have been punished. Yet he did not argue the point.

sentences.zh: 尋除翰林修撰，升待制，以選為國子司業，遂為翰林直學士，階太中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin Compiler, promoted to Attendant Draftsman, selected as Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and then made Direct Hanlin Academician, with rank Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Hanlin compiler, promoted to attendant draftsman, selected as vice chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and then made direct Hanlin academician, with rank grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 端善為政，筮仕湘陰，猾吏束手，不敢舞文法，豪民無賴者遠避去。

translations.literal: Duan was skilled at governing. When he first took office at Xiangyin, crafty clerks held their hands and dared not manipulate the law, and overbearing commoners and ruffians kept far away.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was skilled at governing. When he first took office at Xiangyin, crafty clerks held their hands and dared not manipulate the law, and overbearing commoners and ruffians kept far away.

sentences.zh: 部使者行部，旁郡滯訟，皆諉端讞，端剖決如流，績譽籍然。

translations.literal: When the circuit envoy made his inspection rounds, stalled lawsuits from neighboring prefectures were all referred to Duan for judgment. He decided them like flowing water, and his reputation spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit envoy made his inspection rounds, stalled lawsuits from neighboring prefectures were all referred to Duan for judgment. He decided them like flowing water, and his reputation spread widely.

sentences.zh: 其文章嚴謹有法，寧約近瘠，無奢滋駁。

translations.literal: His literary compositions were strict and disciplined in method, preferring restraint and approaching spareness, without extravagant excess or confusion.
translations.idiomatic: His literary compositions were strict and disciplined in method, preferring restraint and approaching spareness, without extravagant excess or confusion.

sentences.zh: 居翰林久，至順、元統以來，國家崇號，慈極升祔先朝，加封宣聖考妣，制冊多出其手。

translations.literal: He long served in the Hanlin Academy. From the Zhishun and Yuantong reigns onward, when the state honored imperial titles, when the empress dowager of utmost kindness was enshrined with former emperors, and when Confucius's parents received added enfeoffment, many of the edicts and patent letters came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He long served in the Hanlin Academy. From the Zhishun and Yuantong reigns onward, when the state honored imperial titles, when the empress dowager of utmost kindness was enshrined with former emperors, and when Confucius's parents received added enfeoffment, many of the edicts and patent letters came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 預修文宗、明宗、寧宗三朝實錄，及累朝功臣列傳，時稱其有史才。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Wenzong, Mingzong, and Ningzong reigns, and the collected biographies of meritorious ministers of successive reigns. People of the time said he had talent for history.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Wenzong, Mingzong, and Ningzong reigns, and the collected biographies of meritorious ministers of successive reigns. People of the time said he had talent for history.

sentences.zh: 初，文宗建奎章閣，搜羅中外才俊置其中，嘗語阿榮曰：「當今文學之士，朕惟未識謝端。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wenzong established the Kuizhang Pavilion and gathered talented men from within and without to place there, he once told Arong: "Among literary men today, I alone have not yet met Xie Duan."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wenzong established the Kuizhang Pavilion and gathered talented men from within and without to place there, he once told Arong: "Among literary men today, I alone have not yet met Xie Duan."

sentences.zh: 亡何，文宗崩，竟不及用端。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Wenzong died, and in the end Duan was never employed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Wenzong died, and in the end Duan was never employed.

sentences.zh: 端又與趙郡蘇天爵同著《正統論》，辨金、宋正統甚悉，世多傳之。

translations.literal: Duan also co-authored the 《Discourse on Legitimate Succession》 with Su Tianjue of Zhao Commandery, thoroughly arguing the legitimate succession of Jin and Song. The world widely circulated it.
translations.idiomatic: Duan also co-authored the 《Discourse on Legitimate Succession》 with Su Tianjue of Zhao Commandery, thoroughly arguing the legitimate succession of Jin and Song. The world widely circulated it.

sentences.zh: 至元六年卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhizheng reign he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhizheng reign he died, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 元世蜀士以文名者，曰虞集，而謝端其次云。

translations.literal: Among Shu scholars famed for letters in the Yuan, Yu Ji was foremost, and Xie Duan was second.
translations.idiomatic: Among Shu scholars famed for letters in the Yuan, Yu Ji was foremost, and Xie Duan was second.
